alignments.note: Inferential conjunction; the ASV fronts it as clause-initial *For* though the Greek postpositive stands second.

Verbless clause with a locative adverbial predicate: under rule 53 the supplied copula *are* is the predicate's helper, and the relative adverb is what the clause predicates, so the discontinuous *where … are* is one unit under rule 15, headed on *where*. This also keeps the analysis parallel to the answering ἐκεῖ → *there is* in the same verse, which is rule 24's habit. The competing reading gives *are* to ἐριθεία as the nearer conjoined subject under rule 56, on the ground that ὅπου is only a subordinator and the clause has no predicate; I took the predicate reading because ὅπου and ἐκεῖ are a correlative locative pair and each carries its own clause's copula.
Coordinating conjunction joining the two subjects.
Second conjoined subject; the copula stays with the locative predicate under rule 53 rather than with this noun.

Locative adverbial predicate of the verbless main clause, so the supplied *is* is its rule 7 helper under rule 53's adjectival/adverbial case (compare ἐγγύς → *were nigh*). Headed on *there*, the word realizing the adverb; the alternative would put *is* on ἀκαταστασία as the subject noun, which rule 53 refuses when a predicate token is present.
Universal quantifier; no negator stands in the clause, so rule 87 is not in question and it takes its own word.
Attributive adjective; the Greek expresses its head noun πρᾶγμα, so the adjective stands alone on *vile* and no determiner question arises (πᾶν already fills the determiner slot).
Head noun of the phrase, rendered *deed*.

review_notes: Reviewed against the contract; returned unchanged. All 11 source and 13 target IDs partitioned exactly once.

The verse is two verbless clauses; both supplied copulas are placed on the locative adverbs ὅπου and ἐκεῖ as adverbial predicates under rule 53, kept consistent with each other under rule 24. The competing placement of *are* on ἐριθεία (rule 56) is named in the ὅπου unit's note.

The packet's gloss column is the visible evidence for that competing reading: it brackets the existential at s005 (`self-interest [exist]`) and at s006 (`there [will be]`), i.e. it follows English word order in placing *are* after *faction*. Rule 53 refuses to read a supplied copula off word order, and rule 63 blocks the same placement by a second route here, since both clauses have lexical-noun subjects and rule 53's noun-phrase exception is scoped to a subject pronoun. ἐκεῖ is an uncontested rule 53 adverbial predicate (compare ἐγγύς → *were nigh*), and ὅπου is its correlative, so the two clauses get one analysis.
Heads: *where* and *there* realize the adverbs' own lexemes and the supplied copulas ride along as rule 7 helpers, so neither head lands on a copula. Rule 15 licenses both discontinuities.

πᾶν φαῦλον πρᾶγμα splits three-to-three under rule 26. πρᾶγμα is expressed, so rule 58's supplied-determiner question does not arise and φαῦλον stays bare; πᾶν stands with no negator in the clause, so rule 87 is not in question.
No unrepresented, added or noncompositional units: every source token has an English realization and every English token answers to a source token.
